chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Sabbah al-Hadda', from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

O Sabbah! If the man from you intends a journey, he should stand at the door of his house facing the direction he is heading towards, and recite Al-Hamd (Surah al-Fatiha) in front of him, on his right, and on his left; and the two Mu'awwidhat (Surah al-Ikhlas, Surah al-Falaq, and Surah an-Nas - note: text says Mu'awwidhatayn but lists three, or implies the two plus Ikhlas as per the list) in front of him, on his right, and on his left; and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' in front of him, on his right, and on his left; and Ayat al-Kursi in front of him, on his right, and on his left.

Then he should say: 'O Allah! Protect me and protect what is with me, and keep me safe and keep safe what is with me, and deliver me and deliver what is with me with Your excellent and beautiful delivery.'
Allah will protect him and protect what is with him, and keep him safe and keep safe what is with him, and deliver him and deliver what is with him.
Have you not seen the man who is protected but what is with him is not protected, and reaches (the destination) but what is with him does not reach, and is safe but what is with him is not safe?

key_terms.آيَةُ الْكُرْسِيِّ: The Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)
key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two Surahs of protection (Al-Falaq and An-Nus)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, the One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and ritual for a Muslim traveler when leaving their house?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) outlines a comprehensive ritual for travelers, emphasizing the spiritual protection of both the individual and their possessions through the recitation of key Quranic chapters (Al-Fatiha, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas, and Ayat al-Kursi) in specific spatial orientations. The supplication highlights the Shia theological distinction between personal safety and the preservation of one's belongings, reflecting a holistic view of divine guardianship. This practice underscores the importance of integrating Quranic recitation with intentional supplication (dua) as a means of securing blessings (barakah) before embarking on a journey.
